description:
Follow-up to the merged canonical-JOB foundation (issue #289 Step 1; PRs #332,
#339, #341, #350 code and #369 docs). A post-merge code review + blind-spot
audit found that the "this is canonical JOB data, reproducibly built, with
integrity verification" claim has thinner anchors than it appears:

  1. `_project/joinorder/reference_cardinalities.json` is committed, so the
     "113/113 aggregate row hashes matched" oracle result proves future builds
     do not DRIFT -- it does not independently prove the data is canonical JOB.
     The per-table sha256 values and `data_archive_hash` in
     `benchbox/core/joinorder/data_manifest.toml` were generated by the same
     build script that produced the Parquet, so verifying the archive against
     them is circular. The only genuinely external anchor is
     `[provenance] pg_dump_sha256 = 1390a764ee76d03d80fd6743ec7a6e5f22493411967582e4f1ecc2e282c1a59c`
     (and the build log's `md5: df3e976b235288005cb410cea09a115f`), and nobody
     has confirmed those match the checksums Harvard Dataverse PUBLISHES for
     DOI 10.7910/DVN/2QYZBT, file id 3590041 (`imdb_pg11`).

  2. "Reproducible canonical data": the recovery story if the GitHub release
     asset disappears is "rebuild from `_project/joinorder/build-inputs` +
     `_project/scripts/build_joinorder_data.py` + the Dataverse source". But
     Parquet output bytes depend on writer version, compression level,
     row-group sizing, dictionary encoding, and row order. `[provenance]
     duckdb_version = "1.3.2"` is pinned, which suggests the authors know this
     matters -- but the rebuild has not been shown to produce the
     byte-identical archive matching `archive_sha256 = 669c97ce...`. If it is
     not deterministic, the manifest's committed sha256 values are
     un-regenerable and the integrity story needs to switch from
     archive-hash to per-table content verification.

  3. Conversion fidelity is only validated where the 113 JOB queries look.
     Row-count + file-sha256 prove the FILE is stable; they do not prove the
     Postgres -> Parquet conversion preserved NULL-vs-empty-string (the
     retired CSV path needed `csv_null_marker=""` precisely because of this),
     integer width (no int32 truncation on 36M-row `cast_info`, or on
     `name`/`title`/`char_name` ids), or UTF-8 round-trip of non-ASCII IMDb
     titles. Columns no JOB query references -- `md5sum`, `phonetic_code`,
     `name_pcode_*`, `series_years`, `imdb_index`, the nullable int columns --
     are entirely unvalidated.

  4. `data_manifest.toml` carries `archive_sha256`, `data_archive_hash`, and
     `manifest_hash` with no inline explanation of what each one is the hash
     OF (the `.tar.zst` file? the extracted tar? the concatenated table
     contents? the manifest itself?). This is a footgun for anyone touching
     the build pipeline later.

Scope is the build/verification pipeline and provenance docs only. NO changes
to the runtime benchmark (`benchbox/core/joinorder/benchmark.py`,
`benchbox/joinorder.py`) or the shipped queries (`queries.py`). If any phase
surfaces a genuine data mismatch (Phase 1 checksum disagreement, Phase 3
fidelity defect), STOP and escalate -- that means the published archive is not
canonical and the foundation needs rework, which is a separate decision.

Related: `joinorder-redistribution-license-adr` (independent, also
release-relevant), `joinorder-accessibility-and-comparability` (independent),
`joinorder-step1-housekeeping` (independent). Step-2 work
(`joinorder-track2-groundwork`, `joinorder-scale-stress-decision-framework`)
is downstream of a trustworthy canonical foundation and benefits from this.

work_units.notes:
Retrieve the checksums Harvard Dataverse publishes for dataset DOI
10.7910/DVN/2QYZBT, file id 3590041 (`imdb_pg11`). Dataverse exposes
per-file checksums via the dataset landing page and the native API
(e.g. `https://dataverse.harvard.edu/api/access/datafile/3590041?format=original`
headers, or the dataset `:latest` metadata JSON which lists
`dataFile.checksum.type` / `.value`, and `dataFile.md5`). Capture the
retrieval method and the raw published values.

Compare published values against:
  - `data_manifest.toml [provenance] pg_dump_sha256 = 1390a764ee76d03d80fd6743ec7a6e5f22493411967582e4f1ecc2e282c1a59c`
  - the build log's curl-reported `md5: df3e976b235288005cb410cea09a115f`
    and the Dataverse metadata block in
    `joinorder_postgres_oracle_20260512T010726Z/restore-postgres.log`.

Output: new file `_project/joinorder/provenance-attestation.md` recording
(a) the Dataverse DOI / file id / access URL, (b) retrieval date, (c) the
published checksum type(s) and value(s), (d) the matched local values,
(e) the gregrahn_commit pin and a one-line note that the SQL corpus is
pinned to that commit. Add a pointer to this file from
`_project/joinorder/migration-plan.md` and from
`docs/benchmarks/join-order.md` "Data Source".

GATE: if any published checksum does NOT match -> STOP, do not start w2/w3,
escalate (the archive is not the canonical Dataverse pg_dump).

If Dataverse no longer exposes a checksum for that file id, document that
explicitly and treat the curl-captured md5/sha256 in the build log as the
best-available anchor -- but flag it as a weaker guarantee in the
attestation doc and in `open_questions`.
Done: Dataverse publishes MD5
`df3e976b235288005cb410cea09a115f` for file id 3590041; it matches the
local cached pg_dump, whose pinned SHA256 is
`1390a764ee76d03d80fd6743ec7a6e5f22493411967582e4f1ecc2e282c1a59c`.
work_units.summary: Phase 1: cross-check Dataverse-published checksums against the pinned pg_dump hashes; record attestation or escalate

work_units.notes:
ANNOUNCE BEFORE RUNNING: this re-downloads the ~1.2 GB Dataverse pg_dump
and runs a Postgres restore in Docker; expect ~10-20 min per build, two
builds. State the command, expected runtime, and log path; tee output to
`/tmp/joinorder-rebuild-check.log`. If a recent Dataverse download is
already cached under `benchmark_runs/joinorder/`, reuse it for the source
and only re-run the Parquet conversion twice (the conversion is the
determinism-sensitive step).

Run `_project/scripts/build_joinorder_data.py` end-to-end (or its build/
convert subcommand) twice into clean work dirs. For each run compute the
sha256 of the produced `joinorder-imdb-2013-v1.tar.zst` and of every
extracted `*.parquet`. Compare run1 vs run2, and both vs the committed
`archive_sha256 = 669c97ce7e9e7498c7ce0cad018153aa93a9b8eefff0f77e436d690f64ebc5fd`
and the per-table sha256 values in `data_manifest.toml`.

GATE A (byte-identical, matching committed values): record the
reproducibility proof in `_project/joinorder/provenance-attestation.md`
(the exact command, toolchain versions, the matched hashes) and add a
`make`/script target or test note that re-runs the determinism check on
demand. Done.

GATE B (NOT byte-identical): STOP and escalate with a decision question
(AskUserQuestion) between:
  (i) pin the conversion toolchain harder until deterministic -- pyarrow
      and duckdb versions, parquet `row_group_size`, `compression` /
      `compression_level`, dictionary encoding, deterministic row order
      (ORDER BY primary key before write), and pin them in
      `build_joinorder_data.py` + record in `[provenance]`; OR
  (ii) accept that the rebuild produces EQUIVALENT-not-IDENTICAL bytes:
       switch the integrity story so download verification is per-table
       content hash (logical row hash, order-independent) rather than
       `archive_sha256`, and update the manifest schema + docs to say so.
Either path: update `docs/benchmarks/join-order.md` "Data Source" and
`_project/joinorder/release-notes.md` to state the ACTUAL guarantee
("rebuild reproduces the byte-identical archive" vs "rebuild reproduces
logically-equivalent tables verified by per-table content hash").
Done with Gate B triggered: run1 archive
`e24bc0f1a12ab7619942da4b985d2eae809686b0d986005334bada93692e0a49`,
run2 archive
`adf28547f5c2b90884a0e2564cdf8a42b9a1c16192461dcc02a78677e21fa952`,
committed archive
`669c97ce7e9e7498c7ce0cad018153aa93a9b8eefff0f77e436d690f64ebc5fd`.
`cast_info.parquet` differed between run1 and run2, so this TODO was
blocked pending
`_project/TODO/main/planning/joinorder-parquet-rebuild-determinism-decision.yaml`.
Hygiene closeout: that decision is now completed in
`_project/DONE/main/planning/joinorder-parquet-rebuild-determinism-decision.yaml`;
BenchBox documents logical content equivalence rather than
byte-identical archive rebuilds.
work_units.summary: Phase 2: deterministic-rebuild check -- build the archive twice, diff bytes vs committed archive_sha256; record proof or trigger Gate B

work_units.notes:
Add a check (a new `build_joinorder_data.py` subcommand, e.g.
`verify-conversion-fidelity`, or a sibling helper) that runs against the
restored Postgres + the converted Parquet and asserts agreement on the
columns the 113 JOB queries never touch:
  - NULL vs empty string: for nullable `character varying` columns
    (`note`, `md5sum`, `phonetic_code`, `name_pcode_cf`, `name_pcode_nf`,
    `name_pcode_sf`, `surname_pcode`, `imdb_index`, `series_years`,
    `info`), confirm Postgres NULL maps to Parquet null (not "") and
    Postgres '' (if any) maps to "" -- COUNT(*) WHERE col IS NULL must
    match on both sides for each such column.
  - integer width: for every `integer` column on the large tables
    (`cast_info`, `name`, `title`, `char_name`, `movie_info`,
    `movie_keyword`, `person_info`) confirm MIN/MAX fit in int32 and the
    Parquet physical type is INT32 (or INT64 if any value exceeds int32)
    -- i.e. detect silent truncation either direction.
  - UTF-8 round-trip: pick rows with non-ASCII bytes in `title.title`,
    `name.name`, `aka_title.title`, `char_name.name`; compare the exact
    string (or a sha256 of the UTF-8 bytes) Postgres-side vs Parquet-side.
  - row-count parity: COUNT(*) per table matches `data_manifest.toml`
    `row_count` (already done in restore validation; assert it here too so
    the fidelity check is self-contained).
Wire it into the same flow as `verify-reference-results` (so the heavy
Postgres-oracle run exercises it), and add a reduced version to the
DuckDB tiny-fixture test (`tests/unit/core/joinorder/test_canonical_queries.py`
or a sibling) covering the int-width + null-vs-empty assertions on the
tiny tables.

Acceptance: the new check runs in the oracle flow and passes; the
tiny-fixture variant is in `make test-fast`. GATE: if it surfaces a real
mismatch -> STOP, escalate (the Parquet conversion is lossy).
Done: `verify-conversion-fidelity` passed against the restored Postgres
source and rebuilt Parquet with 21 row-count checks, 37 null/empty checks,
59 integer-width checks, and 4 UTF-8 column groups. A tiny-fixture fast
regression covers null preservation and integer-width safety.
work_units.summary: Phase 3: conversion-fidelity validation for columns outside the 113-query workload (NULL/empty, int width, UTF-8); wire into the oracle harness
